text.text_excerpt: Thalia is a great restaurant with seemingly "simple" but well executed food with the highest quality ingredients. It's a very small place, with a small menu, and even a small kitchen but the flavors are big and the portions are a nice size. If you want to leave stuffed you can, but you don't have to! Unsurprisingly the wine list is also small but extremely well chosen with two sparkling Cremants by the glass as well as 3 white and 3 red pours which can pair with just about anything on the menu. Cocktails are also expertly made and there are some unique options despite limited space behind the bar and that the bartender is also acting as server for 8 people at the large and winding bar. I was so excited to try this new restaurant since I've been following them on Instagram and seeing them making progress on getting closer to opening. They also have a partnership with a community garden a couple blocks away that my friend runs so I was excited to see how it turned out! It was wonderful to be there in the opening night. Everyone was so excited and friendly and wanting us to enjoy ourselves! At the end they gave us postcards to write our address on for them to send us a thank you note! This place opened its doors yesterday by the owners of Coquette. I was incredibly impressed. They have a diverse menu of cocktails and food. All pastas have half and full portions. The half was quite filling. I got the chicken pasta and was taken with the creamy flavoring. My friend who doesn't eat a lot of dairy or gluten had a shrimp dish she could enjoy. The staff was very friendly and made us cocktails that weren't on the menu including a drink with an espresso ice cube in it. I would definitely go back to try more of the pastas. The bolognese looked amazing too.
